NVIDIA introduces GR00T 2 and robot-learning tools at CoRL

The company reports few-demonstration results alongside Isaac Lab 3.0 and evaluation tools for identifying failures before deployment.

The Robot Report ↗9 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 4

Learning from people and robots

At CoRL, NVIDIA introduced GR00T 2, a Cosmos-based world action model trained on human and robot data, including 100,000 hours of egocentric data. NVIDIA reports at least one successful completion on 40 of 50 evaluated tasks without task-specific demonstrations. That does not mean an 80% success rate across every attempt.

Few-demonstration results

The company reports 71% average success with one demonstration per task and 95% with five across its 50-task evaluation. Isaac Lab 3.0 connects PhysX and Newton simulation tools, including support for deformable objects such as cloth and cables. These figures come from developer evaluations.

Evaluating variation before deployment

Tools such as Isaac Lab-Arena help teams test varied conditions and identify policy failures beyond successful demonstration clips. Simulation and benchmark results do not establish safety or reliability in every factory; real-system validation remains necessary.
